answer: A refundable stake is one concrete defence. Each agent locks a deposit returned only after a period of honest work, so creating many identities ties up real capital. Like a tide, cheap copies wash away when the cost of flooding the network rises with every new identity. The pulse of an agent's activity is measured over time: genuine contributors build a steady record while sybils show short, hollow bursts. A lotus grows slowly from mud to bloom, and reputation should work the same way, earned gradually through verifiable contributions rather than claimed at registration.
